parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a clean-room reverse engineering benchmark: use only the binary and bundled docs, avoid source reuse, and deliver a new executable matching CLI/LSP behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split early discovery across doc and CLI/LSP child probes while continuing local probing; it retained final integration and verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: After black-box probing RustOwl help, version, completions, check, clean, toolchain, and stdio behavior, the run adopted a child-produced Rust implementation and patched runtime mismatches.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent inspected the child-built workspace, repaired clean/check behavior, refreshed the root executable through compile.sh, cleaned Cargo artifacts, and delivered source plus binary.
parallel.verification: Verification covered help/version/banner output, argument errors, completions, check failure paths, clean behavior, toolchain path effects, and JSON-RPC initialize/shutdown/unsupported-method flows.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final answer acknowledged that deeper successful Rust analysis remained only approximated because the original environment lacked the RustOwl runtime/toolchain; official evaluation failed 570 of 762 passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room constraint and focused on reproducing the executable from observed CLI, documentation, filesystem, and stdio/LSP behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned documentation review, probing, implementation, integration, verification, artifact installation, and final cleanup without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial run first tried a crate-based Rust parser, then switched to a std-only implementation with static completion fixtures and a hand-rolled JSON-RPC/parser layer after offline build failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It created Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, completion fixtures, compile.sh, installed the rebuilt executable, removed build artifacts, and left the final source tree ready.
serial.verification: It performed side-by-side checks for CLI parser/help, completion output, clean side effects including Cargo.lock behavior, toolchain install/uninstall, check failure modes, and multiple LSP edge cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite slightly deeper late verification of LSP and clean edge cases, the implementation still failed the official evaluator with 574 of 762 passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room binary-only reverse-engineering requirement and built a new Rust executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same benchmark requirement and kept the effort to bundled docs plus normal executable interaction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement misunderstanding separates the runs; both targeted the same RustOwl CLI and LSP surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned doc and CLI/LSP probes early, then the parent continued local probing and retained final integration ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, design, implementation, and verification in one agent-owned path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed discovery and implementation assistance; serial traded concurrency for continuous context, but both retained an implementation owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received a child implementation handoff, then the parent audited it against previously captured behavior and patched remaining mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated context directly and converted observed behavior into its own std-only implementation without handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference is handoff versus local continuity; the parallel handoff was consumed rather than lost, stale, or conflicting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed CLI, LSP, check, clean, and toolchain behavior, adopted the child-built implementation, then patched clean and check mismatch handling.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed the same surfaces, switched from crate-based code to a std-only rewrite after dependency fetch failed, and added stricter clean and LSP edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial invested more late effort in LSP initialization/cancellation and clean Cargo.lock behavior; parallel covered a similar but slightly shallower surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited on children, interrupted/resumed one child, and ultimately received and used the implementation result before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and closed from its own final verification state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra lifecycle events, but they did not strand a needed completed result; serial avoided that coordination overhead entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel noticed that the child had built over ./executable, audited that shared-workspace output, then patched and cleaned the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed the root executable from its current sources, reinstalled after a housekeeping fix, and cleaned target artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integration involved adopting shared child writes; serial integration was linear. No unresolved write collision remained in parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel stated it verified help/version/banner, errors, completions, check failure paths, clean, toolchain, and stdio JSON-RPC behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did final smoke checks against a saved reference after matching CLI, protocol, clean, and stateful command behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local black-box checks; serial appears to have checked a few more late edge cases, but both failed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and far more LLM/tool activity, finished within the agent budget, and delivered before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one trajectory, fewer calls, finished faster, and also delivered before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred overhead and noisy child limits, but the run did not time out or close without a deliverable; serial was simpler and slightly faster.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is concordant both_fail, not discordant: parallel failed with 570/762 and serial failed with 574/762. Both implemented a clean-room Rust replacement for the observed RustOwl CLI/LSP surface. The small score gap is best explained by ordinary implementation coverage differences, especially serial probing of additional LSP initialization/cancellation and clean side-effect details, not by a retained parallel coordination failure.
parallel_contributors: Parallel obtained useful child help but also had coordination overhead, a retry-limit child, and a child interruption/resume sequence.
The parent nevertheless consumed the child implementation, patched mismatches, verified locally, and delivered a complete candidate.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all task knowledge in one thread and probed several late edge cases before final installation.
Serial still failed the official evaluator, indicating remaining behavioral gaps unrelated to delegation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial added later clean Cargo.lock and stricter LSP initialization/cancellation behavior that parallel did not clearly cover.
Both runs approximated deeper successful Rust analysis because the observed environment exposed mostly failure paths around missing RustOwl runtime/toolchain pieces.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative explanation for the small testcase-count gap only

Rejected because the parent explicitly consumed the child implementation and patched it into the final workspace.
Rejected because no verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; available useful results reached the parent.
Rejected because failed or limited child activity did not strand required work; the parent continued probing, implementation, patching, and verification itself.
Rejected because the completed implementation result from the child was inspected and used by the parent.
Rejected because the parent polled, listed agents, interrupted/resumed as needed, and continued local work rather than passively waiting to the deadline.
Rejected because the child and parent did not leave competing cross-file designs; parent adoption and patching produced a single final implementation.
Rejected because no live same-file edit conflict or required reconciliation of simultaneous edits is shown.
Rejected because source updates were part of parent integration of a completed child implementation, not a proven replacement of another live owner's non-entry source.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The retry-limit child and later interrupt/resume sequence were treated as coordination noise, not split into early termination, fan-out exhaustion, missing join, or no-takeover labels because the parent consumed useful work and delivered.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate cleared the retention gate for a realized adverse parallel coordination consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained for mere subagent count, ordinary implementation gaps, or the concordant official failure.
